title: Rank and Rent: get your first 5 local SEO clients and reach $10K/month
summary: A step-by-step playbook for using rank and rent sites as a foot in the door for local SEO agencies: pick a service plus city, build a structured site, run a citation and branded-link sequence, then monetize leads via partners and upsell them into full SEO. Covers pricing math, partner sourcing, and pitching channels.

principles.text: Rank and rent solves the no-proof, no-case-study problem: you own a lead-gen asset that earns while you land SEO clients.
principles.quote: Rank and rents give you a way to get your foot in the door while getting paid because rank and rents, how it works is you basically target a service and a city and you build a site

principles.text: Rank and rent isn't limited to local; national keywords can land five-figure clients, but local is easier to rank.
principles.quote: it doesn't have to be, for example, accountant Vancouver. It could be something as broad as a national keyword such as, I don't know, best protein supplement

principles.text: Build city pages for every service and nearby suburb, even where keyword plus city volume looks low; they capture near-me and long-tail searches.
principles.quote: Don't be so focused on, oh, I don't know. This the the search volume for payroll Roundrock isn't very high, so I'm not going to create that service page. It actually works for generalized keywords as well

principles.text: On new sites, keep link building conservative: only 1-2 branded links a month to the homepage, not exact-match anchors.
principles.quote: one to two links a month only branded to the homepage

principles.text: Operators are the real bottleneck, not leads. Cycle through partners fast and keep the dependable ones.
principles.quote: Issue with rank and rents is not the getting leads part. It's that partners aren't dependable.

principles.text: Use pay-per-lead or monthly rental when starting; save percentage-of-revenue deals for proven closers.
principles.quote: if you're starting out I would not do percentage of sale like I mentioned it really comes down to how good of a business owner they are
